Selected work

Engagements and projects, newest first. Open any one for the context, what I built and what changed.

Careers360 · Automation frameworkCypress framework for a CMS platform
35% coverage · 250+ cases

Context

The Careers360 CMS powers educational content: articles, e-books, college and exam data, publishing workflows and role-based access for a platform serving 2M+ monthly users. Regression was manual, slow and inconsistent across environments.

What I built

  • Page Object based Cypress framework from scratch, with modular utilities and reusable commands
  • 250+ test cases across publishing, content modules, permissions and critical business workflows
  • Coverage for 50+ CMS modules, including RBAC and content state transitions
  • Jenkins integration so regression runs on code commits, not just before release

Outcome

  • 35% automation coverage across 250+ test cases
  • ~25% less manual regression effort
  • ~30% shorter release cycle with regression in CI
CypressJavaScriptPOMJenkinsJira
Careers360 · IntegrationCMS → API → LMS data-flow validation
15+ integration points

Context

Content published in the CMS had to appear correctly in the learning platform. Three or more systems were involved — CMS, backend APIs and LMS — with 10K+ concurrent students depending on accurate synchronisation.

What I built

  • Mapped and documented 15+ integration points across CMS, APIs and LMS
  • End-to-end checks that content publishing, updates and unpublishing reached learners correctly
  • Postman API validation for request/response contracts and negative cases
  • SQL/MySQL queries to confirm persisted state on both sides of each hand-off

Outcome

  • Content-sync defects caught before release instead of by learners
  • Faster root-cause isolation across three systems
  • 15+ data-related bugs identified and fixed pre-release

Careers360 · Framework migrationMoving high-value regression to Playwright
−45% regression time

Context

The Cypress suite covered the right workflows but the full regression was getting slower as coverage grew. Release validation needed to fit inside a working day, across multiple browser targets.

What I built

  • Migrated 80+ high-value regression workflows from Cypress to Playwright
  • Parallel execution across 8 browser configurations
  • Reused the Page Object structure so page knowledge stayed in one place
  • Jenkins jobs for nightly and on-demand runs, with artefacts retained per build

Outcome

  • ~45% reduction in regression execution time
  • 80+ workflows running in parallel instead of serially
  • Same coverage, fewer wall-clock hours before a release
PlaywrightJavaScriptPOMJenkinsDocker

Cross-project · API and dataValidating beyond the browser
15+ data defects caught

Context

UI-only testing leaves integration and persistence problems invisible. Several releases depended on data moving correctly between services, so the checks had to go deeper than the screen.

What I built

  • Postman collections covering status codes, payload shape, authentication and negative cases
  • OAuth/JWT and RBAC checks on protected endpoints and roles
  • SQL/MySQL queries for integrity, consistency and orphaned-record checks
  • Correlated UI behaviour, API responses and database rows during defect analysis

Outcome

  • Defects isolated to the correct layer instead of guessed at
  • 15+ data-related bugs found and fixed before release
  • More complete validation than a UI-only regression pass

How the systems fit together

The parts I actually test: content in, APIs in the middle, learners on the other side — and the pipeline that checks it all.

CMS → API → LMS data flow

Content is authored and published in the CMS, served through backend APIs, and consumed by the LMS. Each hand-off is a place where data can drift.

CMSauthoring · publishing · RBAC
→
API layercontracts · auth · payloads
→
Databasepersistence · integrity
→
LMSenrollment · content · progress
✓ UI state matches API response ✓ API response matches persisted row ✓ Published content reaches the right role

Playwright / Cypress delivery pipeline

Automation is only useful if it runs without a person remembering to start it. This is the loop I build around a suite.

Git pushbranch · pull request
→
Jenkinsnightly · on demand
→
Dockerconsistent runtime
→
Playwright / Cypressparallel workers
→
Reports + Jiraevidence · defects

Validation layers

A UI pass alone is not a quality signal. I check the same behaviour at several levels so a failure points at a layer, not a guess.

UIPlaywright and Cypress journeys, assertions on visible state, cross-browser checks
APIPostman and REST Assured: status, schema, auth, negative and boundary cases
DatabaseSQL and MySQL: integrity, consistency, orphaned records, data flow
AccessRBAC, authentication and authorisation across student, editor and admin roles

suite › ai

AI-assisted quality engineering

I use AI where it removes repetitive authoring work and keep it away from the parts that need judgement. No autonomous QA claims here — this is practical, reviewed assistance.

01

Requirement

Read the story and acceptance criteria; identify the risk and the boundaries.

02

Scenario drafting

Use an LLM to propose positive, negative and edge cases, then prune against the requirement.

03

Code assist

Draft and refactor Cypress/Playwright code with Copilot; review every assertion by hand.

04

Failure triage

Summarise sanitised logs into probable causes, then verify against traces and data.

05

Documentation

Draft test notes and defect reports; keep evidence attached and reproducible.

What each tool is actually good for

TaskGitHub CopilotLLM chatManual
Drafting test scenariosLimitedStrong with contextReliable, slower
Writing page objectsStrongUseful draftsFull control
Refactoring selectorsStrongUsefulTime-consuming
Negative and boundary casesLimitedStrong prompts neededJudgement required
Failure triage from logsNot suitedGood first passSlow but authoritative
Final assertion reviewNever trusted aloneNever trusted aloneAlways

Guardrails I keep

Review before execution

No generated test runs before a person has read the assertions and the data it touches.

Verify against the requirement

An assertion is only valid if it maps to acceptance criteria — not to what the model assumed.

Sanitise inputs

No credentials, personal data or confidential source code goes to unapproved AI services.

Treat output as a hypothesis

A likely cause from a model is a starting point for investigation, never proof of a defect.

suite › reporting

Test reporting and results

Evidence that a release decision can be made from: what ran, what failed, why, and where to look.

Cypress reports

Per-spec results, retries and captured screenshots from the runner.

Playwright HTML report

Steps, retries, traces and attachments in one shareable report.

JUnit XML

Machine-readable results that Jenkins can trend across builds.

Screenshots

Captured at the moment a test fails, attached to the result.

Videos

A recording for failures that a screenshot cannot explain.

Playwright traces

Actions, DOM snapshots and network calls, step by step.

Logs

Console, network and framework logs beside each result.

CI artefacts

Reports archived with each Jenkins build so history is not lost.

Execution history

Build-by-build trends in pass rate and duration.

Pass, fail and skip

Counts per run, grouped by suite rather than one blended number.

Failure classification

Each failure marked as product defect, flaky, environment or test issue.

Defect reports

Reproducible steps, expected versus actual, and evidence in Jira.

suite › metrics

Quality engineering metrics

The numbers I use to decide whether testing is working — and the formula behind each one.

Automation coverage

automated scenarios ÷ scenarios in scope

Tracked per suite, so gaps are visible before they become escapes.

35% across 250+ cases

Regression execution time

wall-clock time of the full regression run

Parallel workers and containerised environments keep runs comparable.

−45% after Playwright migration

Test pass rate

passed ÷ executed, per run

Read together with failure causes, never on its own.

Flaky test rate

tests with mixed results on unchanged code ÷ all tests

Flaky tests are fixed or quarantined so a red build keeps its meaning.

Defect leakage

defects found in production ÷ all defects for the release

The measure that shows whether testing caught what mattered.

−20% post-release defects

Defect resolution time

time from report to verified fix

Better triage and reproducible evidence shorten the loop.

−35% through Jira triage

Release cycle time

time from release candidate to validated build

Regression in CI keeps this short and predictable.

−30% with CI regression

Authoring time saved

baseline authoring hours − assisted hours

Only counted where the output was reviewed and merged.

~40% with AI assistance
